verses.restored: Jesus, full of holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led in the Spirit in the wilderness

familiar.text: And Jesus being full of the Holy Ghost returned from Jordan, and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,

modern.text: Then Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit into the wilderness,

original.text: Ἰησοῦς δὲ ⸂πλήρης πνεύματος ἁγίου⸃ ὑπέστρεψεν ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἰορδάνου, καὶ ἤγετο ἐν τῷ πνεύματι ⸂ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ⸃

verses.restored: forty days, being tested by the adversarial one. He ate nothing in those days, and when they were completed, he was hungry.

familiar.text: Being forty days tempted of the devil. And in those days he did eat nothing: and when they were ended, he afterward hungered.

modern.text: where for forty days He was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they had ended, He was hungry.

original.text: ἡμέρας τεσσεράκοντα πειραζόμενος ὑπὸ τοῦ διαβόλου. καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις, καὶ συντελεσθεισῶν ⸀αὐτῶν ἐπείνασεν.

verses.restored: The adversarial one said to him, If you are Son of the Divine, speak to this stone so that it may become bread.

familiar.text: And the devil said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.

modern.text: The devil said to Him, “If You are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”

original.text: ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, εἰπὲ τῷ λίθῳ τούτῳ ἵνα γένηται ἄρτος.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, It has been written: A human does not live by bread alone.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.

modern.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Man shall not live on bread alone.’ ”

original.text: καὶ ἀπεκρίθη ⸂πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ Ἰησοῦς⸃· Γέγραπται ὅτι Οὐκ ἐπʼ ἄρτῳ μόνῳ ζήσεται ⸀ὁ ⸀ἄνθρωπος.

verses.restored: Leading him up, he showed him all the reigns of the inhabited world in a moment of time.

familiar.text: And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time.

modern.text: Then the devil led Him up to a high place and showed Him in an instant all the kingdoms of the world.

original.text: Καὶ ἀναγαγὼν ⸀αὐτὸν ἔδειξεν αὐτῷ πάσας τὰς βασιλείας τῆς οἰκουμένης ἐν στιγμῇ χρόνου·

verses.restored: The adversarial one said to him, I will give you all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.

familiar.text: And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.

modern.text: “I will give You authority over all these kingdoms and all their glory,” he said. “For it has been relinquished to me, and I can give it to anyone I wish.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ διάβολος· Σοὶ δώσω τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην ἅπασαν καὶ τὴν δόξαν αὐτῶν, ὅτι ἐμοὶ παραδέδοται καὶ ᾧ ⸀ἂν θέλω δίδωμι αὐτήν·

verses.restored: Therefore, if you bow/prostrate before me, it will all be yours.

familiar.text: If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.

modern.text: So if You worship me, it will all be Yours.”

original.text: σὺ οὖν ἐὰν προσκυνήσῃς ἐνώπιον ἐμοῦ, ἔσται σοῦ πᾶσα.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, It has been written: You shall bow/prostrate to the Lord your Divine, and him alone shall you serve.

familiar.text: And Jesus answered and said unto him, Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.

modern.text: But Jesus answered, “It is written: ‘Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.’ ”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ⸂ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτῷ⸃· Γέγραπται· ⸂Κύριον τὸν θεόν σου προσκυνήσεις⸃ καὶ αὐτῷ μόνῳ λατρεύσεις.

verses.restored: He led him to Jerusalem and stood him on the pinnacle of the temple and said to him, If you are Son of the Divine, throw yourself down from here.

familiar.text: And he brought him to Jerusalem, and set him on a pinnacle of the temple, and said unto him, If thou be the Son of God, cast thyself down from hence:

modern.text: Then the devil led Him to Jerusalem and set Him on the pinnacle of the temple. “If You are the Son of God,” he said, “throw Yourself down from here.

original.text: ⸂Ἤγαγεν δὲ⸃ αὐτὸν εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ ⸀ἔστησεν ἐπὶ τὸ πτερύγιον τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Εἰ υἱὸς εἶ τοῦ θεοῦ, βάλε σεαυτὸν ἐντεῦθεν κάτω·

verses.restored: For it has been written: He will command his messengers concerning you, to guard you,

familiar.text: For it is written, He shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee:

modern.text: For it is written: ‘He will command His angels concerning You to guard You carefully;

original.text: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ ἐντελεῖται περὶ σοῦ τοῦ διαφυλάξαι σε,

verses.restored: and, On their hands they will lift you up, lest you strike your foot against a stone.

familiar.text: And in their hands they shall bear thee up, lest at any time thou dash thy foot against a stone.

modern.text: and they will lift You up in their hands, so that You will not strike Your foot against a stone.’ ”

original.text: καὶ ⸀ὅτι Ἐπὶ χειρῶν ἀροῦσίν σε μήποτε προσκόψῃς πρὸς λίθον τὸν πόδα σου.

verses.restored: Jesus answered him, It has been said: You shall not test the Lord your Divine.

familiar.text: And Jesus answering said unto him, It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.

modern.text: But Jesus answered, “It also says, ‘Do not put the Lord your God to the test.’ ”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ὅτι Εἴρηται· Οὐκ ἐκπειράσεις κύριον τὸν θεόν σου.

verses.restored: Having completed every test, the adversarial one departed from him until an opportune time.

familiar.text: And when the devil had ended all the temptation, he departed from him for a season.

modern.text: When the devil had finished every temptation, he left Him until an opportune time. Jesus Begins His Ministry (Isaiah 9:1–7; Matthew 4:12–17; Mark 1:14–15)

original.text: καὶ συντελέσας πάντα πειρασμὸν ὁ διάβολος ἀπέστη ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ ἄχρι καιροῦ.

verses.restored: Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee, and a report about him went out through the whole surrounding region.

familiar.text: And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit into Galilee: and there went out a fame of him through all the region round about.

modern.text: Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and the news about Him spread throughout the surrounding region.

original.text: Καὶ ὑπέστρεψεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐν τῇ δυνάμει τοῦ πνεύματος εἰς τὴν Γαλιλαίαν. καὶ φήμη ἐξῆλθεν καθʼ ὅλης τῆς περιχώρου περὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He taught in their synagogues, being glorified by all.

familiar.text: And he taught in their synagogues, being glorified of all.

modern.text: He taught in their synagogues and was glorified by everyone. The Rejection at Nazareth (Isaiah 61:1–11; Matthew 13:53–58; Mark 6:1–6)

original.text: καὶ αὐτὸς ἐδίδασκεν ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς αὐτῶν, δοξαζόμενος ὑπὸ πάντων.

verses.restored: He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. According to his custom, he entered the synagogue on the Sabbath day and stood up to read.

familiar.text: And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up: and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the sabbath day, and stood up for to read.

modern.text: Then Jesus came to Nazareth, where He had been brought up. As was His custom, He entered the synagogue on the Sabbath. And when He stood up to read,

original.text: Καὶ ἦλθεν ⸀εἰς Ναζαρά, οὗ ἦν τεθραμμένος, καὶ εἰσῆλθεν κατὰ τὸ εἰωθὸς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ τῶν σαββάτων εἰς τὴν συναγωγήν, καὶ ἀνέστη ἀναγνῶναι.

verses.restored: The scroll of the prophet Isaiah was given to him. Unrolling the scroll, he found the place where it was written:

familiar.text: And there was delivered unto him the book of the prophet Esaias. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written,

modern.text: the scroll of the prophet Isaiah was handed to Him. Unrolling it, He found the place where it was written:

original.text: καὶ ἐπεδόθη αὐτῷ βιβλίον ⸂τοῦ προφήτου Ἠσαΐου⸃ καὶ ⸀ἀναπτύξας τὸ βιβλίον εὗρεν τὸν τόπον οὗ ἦν γεγραμμένον·

verses.restored: Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he anointed me to announce good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to send away the oppressed in release,

familiar.text: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor; he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised,

modern.text: “The Spirit of the Lord is on Me, because He has anointed Me to preach good news to the poor. He has sent Me to proclaim liberty to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to release the oppressed,

original.text: Πνεῦμα κυρίου ἐπʼ ἐμέ, οὗ εἵνεκεν ἔχρισέν με εὐαγγελίσασθαι πτωχοῖς, ἀπέσταλκέν ⸀με κηρύξαι αἰχμαλώτοις ἄφεσιν καὶ τυφλοῖς ἀνάβλεψιν, ἀποστεῖλαι τεθραυσμένους ἐν ἀφέσει,

verses.restored: to proclaim the favorable year of the Lord.

familiar.text: To preach the acceptable year of the Lord.

modern.text: to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”

original.text: κηρύξαι ἐνιαυτὸν κυρίου δεκτόν.

verses.restored: Rolling up the scroll, giving it back to the attendant, he sat down. The eyes of all in the synagogue were fixed on him.

familiar.text: And he closed the book, and he gave it again to the minister, and sat down. And the eyes of all them that were in the synagogue were fastened on him.

modern.text: Then He rolled up the scroll, returned it to the attendant, and sat down. The eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed on Him,

original.text: καὶ πτύξας τὸ βιβλίον ἀποδοὺς τῷ ὑπηρέτῃ ἐκάθισεν· καὶ πάντων ⸂οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ⸃ ἦσαν ἀτενίζοντες αὐτῷ.

verses.restored: He began to say to them, Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.

familiar.text: And he began to say unto them, This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.

modern.text: and He began by saying, “Today this Scripture is fulfilled in your hearing.”

original.text: ἤρξατο δὲ λέγειν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Σήμερον πεπλήρωται ἡ γραφὴ αὕτη ἐν τοῖς ὠσὶν ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: All were bearing witness to him and marveling at the words of favor coming from his mouth, and they said, Is this not Joseph's son?

familiar.text: And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph’s son?

modern.text: All spoke well of Him and marveled at the gracious words that came from His lips. “Isn’t this the son of Joseph?” they asked.

original.text: καὶ πάντες ἐμαρτύρουν αὐτῷ καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ἐπὶ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς χάριτος τοῖς ἐκπορευομένοις ἐκ τοῦ στόματος αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον· ⸂Οὐχὶ υἱός ἐστιν Ἰωσὴφ οὗτος⸃;

verses.restored: He said to them, Surely you will say to me this parable: Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we heard happened in Capernaum, do here also in your homeland.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country.

modern.text: Jesus said to them, “Surely you will quote this proverb to Me: ‘Physician, heal yourself! Do here in Your hometown what we have heard that You did in Capernaum.’”

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Πάντως ἐρεῖτέ μοι τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην· Ἰατρέ, θεράπευσον σεαυτόν· ὅσα ἠκούσαμεν γενόμενα ⸂εἰς τὴν Καφαρναοὺμ⸃ ποίησον καὶ ὧδε ἐν τῇ πατρίδι σου.

verses.restored: He said, Amen, I say to you: no prophet is accepted in the prophet's homeland.

familiar.text: And he said, Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country.

modern.text: Then He added, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his hometown.

original.text: εἶπεν δέ· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς προφήτης δεκτός ἐστιν ἐν τῇ πατρίδι αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: In truth I say to you, there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when heaven was shut three years and six months and a great famine came over all the land.

familiar.text: But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land;

modern.text: But I tell you truthfully that there were many widows in Israel in the time of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three and a half years and great famine swept over all the land.

original.text: ἐπʼ ἀληθείας δὲ λέγω ὑμῖν, πολλαὶ χῆραι ἦσαν ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Ἠλίου ἐν τῷ Ἰσραήλ, ὅτε ἐκλείσθη ὁ οὐρανὸς ⸀ἐπὶ ἔτη τρία καὶ μῆνας ἕξ, ὡς ἐγένετο λιμὸς μέγας ἐπὶ πᾶσαν τὴν γῆν,

verses.restored: Yet Elijah was sent to none of them except to Zarephath in Sidon, to a widow woman.

familiar.text: But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow.

modern.text: Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but to the widow of Zarephath in Sidon.

original.text: καὶ πρὸς οὐδεμίαν αὐτῶν ἐπέμφθη Ἠλίας εἰ μὴ εἰς Σάρεπτα τῆς ⸀Σιδωνίας πρὸς γυναῖκα χήραν.

verses.restored: There were many with skin disease in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet, and none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.

familiar.text: And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.

modern.text: And there were many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet. Yet not one of them was cleansed—only Naaman the Syrian.”

original.text: καὶ πολλοὶ λεπροὶ ἦσαν ⸂ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ ἐπὶ Ἐλισαίου τοῦ προφήτου⸃, καὶ οὐδεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκαθαρίσθη, εἰ μὴ Ναιμὰν ὁ Σύρος.

verses.restored: All in the synagogue were filled with rage when they heard these things.

familiar.text: And all they in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath,

modern.text: On hearing this, all the people in the synagogue were enraged.

original.text: καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν πάντες θυμοῦ ἐν τῇ συναγωγῇ ἀκούοντες ταῦτα,

modern.text: They got up, drove Him out of the town, and led Him to the brow of the hill on which the town was built, in order to throw Him over the cliff.

original.text: καὶ ἀναστάντες ἐξέβαλον αὐτὸν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἤγαγον αὐτὸν ἕως ὀφρύος τοῦ ὄρους ἐφʼ οὗ ἡ πόλις ⸂ᾠκοδόμητο αὐτῶν, ὥστε⸃ κατακρημνίσαι αὐτόν·

verses.restored: But he passed through the middle of them and went away.

familiar.text: But he passing through the midst of them went his way,

modern.text: But Jesus passed through the crowd and went on His way. Jesus Expels an Unclean Spirit (Mark 1:21–28)

original.text: αὐτὸς δὲ διελθὼν διὰ μέσου αὐτῶν ἐπορεύετο.

verses.restored: He went down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and was teaching them on the Sabbaths.

familiar.text: And came down to Capernaum, a city of Galilee, and taught them on the sabbath days.

modern.text: Then He went down to Capernaum, a town in Galilee, and on the Sabbath He began to teach the people.

original.text: Καὶ κατῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναοὺμ πόλιν τῆς Γαλιλαίας. καὶ ἦν διδάσκων αὐτοὺς ἐν τοῖς σάββασιν·

verses.restored: They were struck with wonder at his teaching, because his word was with authority.

familiar.text: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for his word was with power.

modern.text: They were astonished at His teaching, because His message had authority.

original.text: καὶ ἐξεπλήσσοντο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ, ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ ἦν ὁ λόγος αὐτοῦ.

modern.text: In the synagogue there was a man possessed by the spirit of an unclean demon. He cried out in a loud voice,

familiar.text: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art; the Holy One of God.

modern.text: “Ha! What do You want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have You come to destroy us? I know who You are—the Holy One of God!”

original.text: ⸀Ἔα, τί ἡμῖν καὶ σοί, Ἰησοῦ Ναζαρηνέ; ἦλθες ἀπολέσαι ἡμᾶς; οἶδά σε τίς εἶ, ὁ ἅγιος τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Jesus rebuked it, saying, Be silent and come out from him. Throwing him into the middle, the troubling spirit came out from him, harming him nothing.

familiar.text: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him. And when the devil had thrown him in the midst, he came out of him, and hurt him not.

modern.text: But Jesus rebuked the demon. “Be silent!” He said. “Come out of him!” At this, the demon threw the man down before them all and came out without harming him.

original.text: καὶ ἐπετίμησεν αὐτῷ ὁ Ἰησοῦς λέγων· Φιμώθητι καὶ ἔξελθε ⸀ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ. καὶ ῥίψαν αὐτὸν τὸ δαιμόνιον εἰς ⸀τὸ μέσον ἐξῆλθεν ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ μηδὲν βλάψαν αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Amazement came upon all, and they spoke with one another, saying, What is this word? For with authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out.

familiar.text: And they were all amazed, and spake among themselves, saying, What a word is this! for with authority and power he commandeth the unclean spirits, and they come out.

modern.text: All the people were overcome with amazement and asked one another, “What is this message? With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”

original.text: καὶ ἐγένετο θάμβος ἐπὶ πάντας, καὶ συνελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Τίς ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὅτι ἐν ἐξουσίᾳ καὶ δυνάμει ἐπιτάσσει τοῖς ἀκαθάρτοις πνεύμασιν, καὶ ἐξέρχονται;

verses.restored: A report about him went out into every place of the surrounding region.

familiar.text: And the fame of him went out into every place of the country round about.

modern.text: And the news about Jesus spread throughout the surrounding region. Jesus Heals at Peter’s House (Matthew 8:14–17; Mark 1:29–34)

original.text: καὶ ἐξεπορεύετο ἦχος περὶ αὐτοῦ εἰς πάντα τόπον τῆς περιχώρου.

familiar.text: And he arose out of the synagogue, and entered into Simon’s house. And Simon’s wife’s mother was taken with a great fever; and they besought him for her.

modern.text: After Jesus had left the synagogue, He went to the home of Simon, whose mother-in-law was suffering from a high fever. So they appealed to Jesus on her behalf,

original.text: Ἀναστὰς δὲ ⸀ἀπὸ τῆς συναγωγῆς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν Σίμωνος. πενθερὰ δὲ τοῦ Σίμωνος ἦν συνεχομένη πυρετῷ μεγάλῳ, καὶ ἠρώτησαν αὐτὸν περὶ αὐτῆς.

modern.text: and He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. And she got up at once and began to serve them.

original.text: καὶ ἐπιστὰς ἐπάνω αὐτῆς ἐπετίμησεν τῷ πυρετῷ, καὶ ἀφῆκεν αὐτήν· παραχρῆμα δὲ ἀναστᾶσα διηκόνει αὐτοῖς.

verses.restored: When the sun was setting, all who had any sick with various diseases brought them to him. Placing hands on each one, he healed them.

familiar.text: Now when the sun was setting, all they that had any sick with divers diseases brought them unto him; and he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them.

modern.text: At sunset, all who were ill with various diseases were brought to Jesus, and laying His hands on each one, He healed them.

original.text: Δύνοντος δὲ τοῦ ἡλίου ⸀ἅπαντες ὅσοι εἶχον ἀσθενοῦντας νόσοις ποικίλαις ἤγαγον αὐτοὺς πρὸς αὐτόν· ὁ δὲ ἑνὶ ἑκάστῳ αὐτῶν τὰς χεῖρας ⸂ἐπιτιθεὶς ἐθεράπευεν⸃ αὐτούς.

verses.restored: Unclean spirits also came out from many, crying out and saying, You are the Son of the Divine. Rebuking them, he did not allow them to speak, because they knew him to be the Messiah.

familiar.text: And devils also came out of many, crying out, and saying, Thou art Christ the Son of God. And he rebuking them suffered them not to speak: for they knew that he was Christ.

modern.text: Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But He rebuked the demons and would not allow them to speak, because they knew He was the Christ. Jesus Preaches in Judea (Mark 1:35–39)

original.text: ἐξήρχετο δὲ καὶ δαιμόνια ἀπὸ πολλῶν ⸀κραυγάζοντα καὶ λέγοντα ὅτι Σὺ ⸀εἶ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ. καὶ ἐπιτιμῶν οὐκ εἴα αὐτὰ λαλεῖν, ὅτι ᾔδεισαν τὸν χριστὸν αὐτὸν εἶναι.

verses.restored: When day came, he went out and traveled to a deserted place. The crowds were seeking him and came to him, and they were trying to hold him back so he would not go away from them.

familiar.text: And when it was day, he departed and went into a desert place: and the people sought him, and came unto him, and stayed him, that he should not depart from them.

modern.text: At daybreak, Jesus went out to a solitary place, and the crowds were looking for Him. They came to Him and tried to keep Him from leaving.

original.text: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἔρημον τόπον· καὶ οἱ ὄχλοι ἐπεζήτουν αὐτόν, καὶ ἦλθον ἕως αὐτοῦ, καὶ κατεῖχον αὐτὸν τοῦ μὴ πορεύεσθαι ἀπʼ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But he said to them, It is necessary for me to announce the good news of the reign of the Divine to the other cities also, because for this I was sent.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.

modern.text: But Jesus told them, “I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent.”

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς ὅτι Καὶ ταῖς ἑτέραις πόλεσιν εὐαγγελίσασθαί με δεῖ τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, ὅτι ⸀ἐπὶ τοῦτο ⸀ἀπεστάλην.

verses.restored: He was proclaiming in the synagogues of Judea.

familiar.text: And he preached in the synagogues of Galilee.

modern.text: And He continued to preach in the synagogues of Judea.

original.text: καὶ ἦν κηρύσσων ⸂εἰς τὰς συναγωγὰς⸃ τῆς ⸀Ἰουδαίας.
